pass1.sentence: A value of 90 or above is normal only if there is no other sign of kidney damage;
pass1.note: kidney.org (KDIGO-based): G1 is eGFR 90 or above AND kidney damage; 90+ alone is not CKD.

pass1.sentence: a value below 60 for three months or more defines chronic kidney disease,
pass1.note: kidney.org: eGFR below 60 for 3 months or more; existing creatinine-egfr record cites NG203 (>90 days).
NICE search summary: an eGFR of less than 15 (category G5) is referred to as kidney failure.

pass1.sentence: Chronic kidney disease, graded from G3a to G5 by the value
pass1.note: kidney.org: G3a eGFR 45-59 ... G5 below 15. G3b/G4 limits not retrieved in pass 1 and not written.

pass1.sentence: A substantial share of kidney function can be lost before creatinine leaves the normal range.
pass1.note: Reviews (ICU review, StatPearls) say up to about 50% can be lost; figure not UK-guideline, so wording kept qualitative.
